sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's JETP and domestic carbon market are funneling capital into geothermal and green hydrogen, making PGEO and BREN structural winners regardless of global rate cycles.
US climate-tech weakness is a valuation reset, not a demand collapse, but Indonesian names with local revenue and government contracts offer superior risk-adjusted returns.
Green industrial transition in chemicals (TPIA) and waste-to-energy (CDIA) is accelerating on domestic regulation, creating durable earnings growth independent of US policy.
sectors.ai: Buy the dip in Indonesian geothermal and green industrial names (PGEO, CDIA, BREN) as domestic policy tailwinds and JETP funding offset US rate-driven weakness. Trim US-exposed climate tech, rotate into IDX-listed renewables with proven cash flows; watch TPIA for chemical transition upside.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small/mid-cap FMCG names are driving sector returns as institutional investors rotate out of large-cap staples into higher-beta consumer plays with clearer earnings catalysts.
Water and beverage companies (ADES, AGAR) are benefiting from structural demand growth in premium hydration and on-the-go consumption, supported by rising urban disposable income.
Packaging and plastics-linked consumer firms (PDES, INDR) are gaining on input-cost stabilization and export-driven volume recovery, offering durable margin expansion into 2025.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small/mid-cap FMCG names showing volume-price breakouts (PDES, ADES, AGAR) while large caps lag; momentum is broad but fragile, so take profits on 10%+ single-day spikes. Favor water/beverage and packaging sub-sectors for earnings visibility; avoid chasing BTEK without confirmation. Position for a 2-4 week hold as IDX consumer breadth improves, but trim if aggregate signal flips negative.

SMGR's steady advance signals cement demand is firming ahead of the election-year infrastructure push. Trim US-exposed names like VRT on rate-cut delays; rotate into domestic contractors with visible government backlog.

Indonesia healthcare lags on macro, so rotate capital to US names for 3-6 months; avoid ID exposure until rupiah stabilizes.

sectors.name: Logistics

Consolidation in the freight forwarding segment favors larger players like GTSI and ELPI, as smaller operators face margin compression from fuel costs and digitalization pressures.

Rotate out of laggards like BLTA and SAFE into names with port/commodity exposure. Expect consolidation near current levels, but add on any 3-5% dip as ID logistics outperformance persists through Q3.
